column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not envy one another, do not inflate prices against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and do not undercut one another in selling. Be, O servants of Allah, brothers.

The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, forsake him, lie to him or hold him in contempt. Taqwā is here”—and he pointed to his chest three times. “It is evil enough for a person to hold his Muslim brother in contempt. All of the Muslim is inviolable to the Muslim: his blood, his wealth and his honour.” Reported by Muslim.

Lā taḥāsadū (“do not envy one another”): let none of you envy another. Wa-lā tanājashū (“do not inflate prices against one another”): let no one who does not want to buy an item raise its price in order to deceive someone else. Wa-lā tabāghaḍū (“do not hate one another”): do not cut one another off out of hatred. Lā tadābarū (“do not turn your backs on one another”): each turning away from the other out of hatred.

Lā yaẓlimuhu (“he does not wrong him”): he does not bring harm upon his brother. Wa-lā yakhdhuluhu (“or forsake him”): by not supporting him. Wa-lā yakdhibuhu (“or lie to him”): by telling him something contrary to what is apparent and the facts. Wa-lā yaḥqiruhu (“or hold him in contempt”): he does not belittle him. “It is evil enough for a person”: it suffices him as evil. ʿIrḍuhu (“his honour”): his standing and his merits.
The prohibition of envy, mutual hatred, turning one's back on one another and undercutting another's sale.
The prohibition of harming the Muslims in any way, by word, deed or gesture.
The prohibition of what brings about mutual hatred, and the command to do what brings about harmony and unity.
The printed text reads التباس (“confusion”), evidently for التباغض (“mutual hatred”).
The prohibition of injustice; supporting a Muslim and helping him when his Muslim brother needs it; and not belittling or humiliating him.
The heart is the foundation of taqwā, and the limbs follow it.
The inviolability of the blood, wealth and honour of the Muslims, except by right.
This hadith contains praiseworthy manners and virtuous character for whoever is granted success.

In this hadith the noble Prophet ﷺ guides us to what is obligatory on us, the company of Muslims: that we love one another, be united and deal with one another well, in accordance with the Sharīʿah, in a way that leads us to noble character, keeps us far from bad character,

removes hatred from our hearts and makes our dealings with one another lofty, free of envy, injustice, deceit and other things that bring harm and division; for a Muslim's harming his brother is unlawful, whether through wealth, dealings, hand or tongue.
All of the Muslim is inviolable to the Muslim: his blood, his wealth and his honour. Might and honour lie only in taqwā. On the meaning of these lofty manners it has been said:
Noble qualities are chapters arranged in order: / intelligence is the first of them, and silence the second;
knowledge the third, forbearance the fourth, / generosity the fifth, and truthfulness the sixth;
patience the seventh, gratitude the eighth, / gentleness the ninth, and righteousness the tenth.
Another poet:
The most unjust of the people of the earth is one who envies / someone who spends his nights enjoying his blessings.
